introduction: Washington WIC offers nutritious foods and nutrition support through local clinics. WIC eligibility is separate from SNAP and Apple Health.
description: Washington WIC offers nutritious foods and nutrition support through local clinics. WIC eligibility is separate from SNAP and Apple Health.

sections.who: Participants include pregnant or recently postpartum people, breastfeeding participants, infants and children under five. Household income and clinic assessment matter; U.S. citizenship is not required.
sections.get: The clinic assigns food benefits and nutrition services. Caregivers can enroll eligible young children.
sections.docs:
• Ask the clinic which identity, address and income records to bring.
  • Child or pregnancy details for certification.
sections.apply:
1. Find a clinic

    Use Apply for WIC or call 800-841-1410.

  2. Book certification

    Call the clinic and confirm remote or in-person options.

  3. Complete assessment

    Staff review eligibility and explain benefits.
sections.after: Attend follow-up appointments. A change in another benefit program does not automatically end WIC.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using DOH WIC intake; WIC eligibility. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Can a grandparent enroll a child?
Caregivers may enroll eligible children under five.
Washington DOH says U.S. citizenship is not required.
Do I need a clinic appointment?
Yes. Arrange certification with the clinic.
Does loss of SNAP automatically end WIC?
No. WIC has separate eligibility rules.
